contracts.title: Relay link and pairing physical connection
contracts.contract: The established link creates the WebSocket before constructing its crypto session, sends the relay-auth credential before onOpen, requires the expected phone hello, then starts E2EE. URL construction replaces the pathname but preserves existing query/hash; relay-server rejects query strings, so canonical-origin validation belongs upstream. Incoming frames serialize. Socket error waits 250 ms for a typed close; explicit close cancels that timer and disposes once. There is no link-owned overall authentication deadline. Constructor failure after socket creation, or a throwing onError callback before socket.close, can strand cleanup. The separate pairing physical client waits on authentication before starting request timers; its initial authentication send lacks the established link's catch. A caller deadline must not be inferred from a later per-request timeout.
testObligations: Auth send exception; silent socket/hello never arrives; typed close vs 1006; callback throws; explicit close during 250ms grace; upstream URL query refusal.
contracts.downstreamBoundary: RP-M1 owns pairing journal/keychain and candidate provisioning; callers own a total dial budget. Crypto key schedule/client-session internals remain external source boundaries.

contracts.title: Physical E2EE state and queue
contracts.contract: The channel moves awaiting-ready → awaiting-authenticated → ready, binds the transcript hash and authentication keys, and converts encrypted rejection to MobileE2EEAuthenticationError. A generation fences deferred binary decode. Plaintext queues until encryption at actual send, preserving counter order across queued and live output. Overflow reports an error, but sendReady still returns true after enqueue; the actual overflow test asserts all 65 one-megabyte sends return true and one error callback. dispose invalidates generation and clears queues, but does not set a closed protocol state; outer link ownership supplies the closed guard. Neither an error callback nor a true send return proves delivery or peer authentication.
testObligations: Transcript mismatch; queued encryption order; delayed binary vs text; queue overflow with truthful delivery classification; dispose before ready/after ready; replay/tampered frames in both peers.
contracts.downstreamBoundary: Cryptographic primitives, secure storage and native WebSocket implementations retain their own source/test owners; no universal E2EE proof.

contracts.title: Stream ownership and generated cancellation payloads
contracts.contract:
Request-to-stream maps and numeric stream IDs own listeners/snapshots; metadata accepts numbers without integer/finite refinement, and only one browser stream is active. Waiting subscription cancellation suppresses late send; failed send/error removes in finally. End delivery calls the listener before removal without finally, so a throwing end listener can retain state. clear is local only; relay session close clears streams while fail does not.
Terminal cancellation uses its dedicated unsubscribe payload builder. Other relay cancellations require response metadata.subscriptionId, derive method.replace(/\.subscribe$/, '.unsubscribe'), and send only {subscriptionId}; send failure is ignored and local state removed. Direct transport instead uses method-specific builders and delayed ready cleanup: session.tabs needs worktree, agentSession needs sessionId, nativeChat can derive agent:sessionId, and browser uses browser.screencast.unsubscribe. Current session-tabs/native-chat streams do not supply the metadata needed by generic relay cleanup; a name match is not successful cancellation. A browser relay cancellation can resend browser.screencast with a subscription ID instead of invoking unsubscribe. Receivers differ: accounts/notifications/browser use raw IDs; runtime.clientEvents checks the connection prefix; terminal checks ownership; structured/native/session-tabs derive connection-scoped identity. These are source behaviors to preserve as baseline and explicitly adjudicate before intended correction.
testObligations: For every eight cleanup names, assert actual sent method + complete payload + correct owner + receiver state removal; cancel before ready/after ready/after migration; wrong-connection ID; end listener throws; relay fail vs close; false send remains delivery-unknown.
contracts.downstreamBoundary: E3 owns receiver schemas/domain parameter registry; this report joins actual handlers and cleanup semantics, without duplicating that registry.

contracts.title: Finite mobile caller-to-authenticated receiver join
contracts.contract:
Reconstruct the accepted 209-name lower bound from 156 literal names, seven additional conditional names (eight alternatives across four sites), 45 wrapper additions and the bare capability call, then add six previously unlisted subscribe-suffix cleanup names and one direct browser cleanup name: 216 finite names. All 216 have a current allowlist literal and an actual E3 handler range; the companion records canonical caller evidence and per-receiver hashes. This is a bounded construction, not proof against arbitrary future string-valued calls.
Stable logical clients reject closed/suspended work, generation-fence replies and await replacement authentication (12s) before swapping; they replay subscriptions, reject pending requests on cutover and do not replay mutating requests automatically. Projection changes only the supported worktree.ps capability field. Direct requests spend the 30s budget across connection wait and reply, distinguish known nondelivery from timed-out unknown delivery, and honor failWhenDisconnected. Relay session uses hello/version, exact endpoint-host schema, advisory capability settlement and per-frame device token; it does not implement every direct tracker option. Host WebSocket dispatch validates token against the bound token/registry, applies the mobile allowlist, then supplies authenticated fingerprint/client/device/scope/capabilities/connection/signal context before E3 method validation. Registration and allowlisting are separate from authentication and resource ownership. JSON null can reach unguarded property access. Long-poll admission releases in finally. Domain handlers retain structured-session caller/fence checks, terminal driver/query authority, workspace/path grants, Git/provider host selection, settings persistence and UI ownership; see exact E3 handler references.
testObligations: 216-name caller/receiver fixtures without weakening payload schemas; wrong/revoked token; connection-scoped cancellation; direct↔relay migration with pending mutation; timeout nondelivery vs unknown; old→new and new→old wire; authenticated receive after reconnect.
contracts.downstreamBoundary: D-MOBILE-DYNAMIC remains an explicit generic string-input boundary outside the accepted callsite allocation, not an exhaustive whole-application call graph; E3 final usage/push work and E1 UI remain independently owned.

contracts.title: Host execution, external automations and workspace state
contracts.contract:
Exec accepts a nonempty binary, stringifies array args, accepts an optional nonempty cwd, optional string stdin and object env merged with unattended/Git guards. Numeric timeout clamps 1–300s (NaN is not rejected). Windows batch routing refuses shell metacharacters and invokes cmd /d /s /c. The 4MiB cap is per output stream; cap/abort/cancel request kill, while timeout can settle before physical close. Cancellation has no handler-owned auth and execution lanes key by operation/cwd rather than client, so same-lane supersession can cross clients. UTF-8 is decoded per chunk. A true cancellation return is a request acknowledgment.
External automation defaults any non-openclaw provider to Hermes, validates job IDs and four actions, limits create/edit to Hermes, trims prompt/schedule and builds explicit cron argv. execFile has a 30s timeout; count caches clear only after success. No context signal or auth is added by these handlers.
Workspace state uses host home/.orca/sessions, sanitized/truncated namespace and caller-supplied client identity. Missing/corrupt reads become revision zero. Patch checks a finite Number(baseRevision), so absent/NaN bypasses stale revision checks; outer replacement object is only shallowly validated. mkdir0700/write0600/temp rename occurs before publication, without fsync or cross-process lock; publication can throw after durable mutation. Presence TTL45s is pruned on calls, not by timer; namespace maps remain.
testObligations: Cross-client exec lane cancellation; timeout/cap and physical exit observation; Windows quoting; automation CLI failure preserves cache; workspace NaN/absent revision and namespace collision; concurrent/crash writes; publish throws after rename.
contracts.downstreamBoundary: Provider CLIs and their credential/config readers are host-owned imported boundaries. Workspace test titled atomic only asserts revision/publication; it does not prove crash atomicity.

contracts.title: Relay filesystem mutation, watching and stream state
contracts.contract:
Ordinary filesystem mutations deliberately do not enforce RelayContext roots for compatibility. Paths expand host tilde. write rejects a directory via lstat then writes UTF-8 (symlinks can be followed, no atomic replace); deletion uses stat and recursive guards; create-file uses wx after parent mkdir; rename/copy can partially affect state and noClobber checks have a race window. Watch removal coordinates directory deletion.
Terminal-artifact mutation separately checks expected canonical path and stat identity, maximum bytes, no-follow support, hardlink count and a freshly opened handle before rename; the final rename gap is not a transaction. Watch registry normalizes roots, checks client ownership/staleness, shares pending setup, bounds capacity and setup retries, and generation-fences callbacks. unwatchAndWait refuses another live client; fire-and-forget unwatch/dispose does not prove watcher closure. Cancellation during setup releases admission.
FS stream IDs are global numeric IDs without a client owner; ack validates finite numbers but not all sequence/integer constraints. cancel aborts the pump, not immediate physical close; disposal catches close failures. Git response flow receives clientId, unlike FS stream cancellation. File listing retains coalescing/cancellation, and search fallback is restricted to RipgrepUnavailableError.
testObligations: Symlink/hardlink grant swap; noClobber race/partial copy; wrong-client watcher removal; setup cancelled while pending; numeric stream ID cross-client ack/cancel; abort vs pump/handle closure; unavailable ripgrep vs real search error.
contracts.downstreamBoundary: Filesystem/native watcher and shared safe path operations are explicit downstream implementation boundaries; accepted install/build followup owns ripgrep provisioning.

contracts.title: Relay Git mutation and Git2.25 compatibility
contracts.contract:
Git runs on the relay host and deliberately ignores RelayContext roots. Mutation caches invalidate before/finally. Literal pathspec staging uses -- and chunks bulk operations (partial success is possible). Commit trims a required message and returns its nested success/error convention; checkout validates branch/no leading dash; merge/rebase abort methods add no cancellation context. Discard proves lexical containment, but any tracked-probe failure takes the untracked path through shared safe Git clean; it is not raw filesystem deletion.
Fetch serializes shared HEAD work; remote/ref targets are validated, review refs bind a remote URL hash, and GitLab's head/ref aliases remain. Push supports explicit/origin HEAD and force-with-lease only. Pull/fast-forward cancellation can stop lock acquisition without aborting an already-started inner Git command. Rebase uses a 60s controller, unique private ref, old-Git fallback, termination barrier and best-effort private-ref cleanup. Generic exec validates subcommands/config/global flags, but a read-only comment is not authority: branch <new> passes its destructive-flag filter and mutates. Clone emits bounded progress/tails and sends child.kill on abort; no own total timeout/escalation or immediate already-aborted check is established.
Worktree add preserves platform long paths, --no-track/new branch and optional no-checkout; base/push configuration errors warn with narrow unset handling. Git2.25 list-format fallback is cached per handler and loses newline-path expressiveness; normal list errors propagate, while remove catches failed list to [] and loses preliminary lock/branch metadata. Removal fences watchers and re-proves submodule cleanliness before force, preserves a branch on safe-delete failure, and only forces deletion with explicit policy. Local-base refresh validates ref ownership/ancestry and tracked cleanliness, uses reset --hard for checked-out branches and compare-and-swap update-ref otherwise. Force branch deletion verifies expected HEAD and checkout state before/after, attempts restoration on a race and cleans config best-effort.
testObligations: Real Git2.25 and modern Git; abort during lock vs command; bulk partial effects; network failure during tracked probe; generic branch creation; stale worktree metadata/locked submodule; compare-and-swap branch race and restoration failure; clone cancellation with live descendant.
contracts.downstreamBoundary: Shared merge proofs, safe-clean/pathspec helpers and Git credential/network transports remain WP-ENG-GIT owner boundaries; no recursive re-audit of every imported helper.

contracts.title: PTY creation, ownership, revival and delivery
contracts.contract:
Spawn validates operation identity/capacity and deduplicates by operation ID, not client; unknown outcomes after physical spawn stay fenced against duplicate creation. Agent/surface claims and expected owner/incarnation matter before native work. Abort/stale checks precede spawn; host/WSL cwd, shell, environment and history follow platform ownership. Fresh PTYs record an epoch/incarnation and authenticated owner when supplied. Attach validates pane/tab identity, replay/recovery barriers and retired surfaces; missing pooled state is not exit proof.
Legacy data/resize notifications add no context ownership; resize clamps 1..500 and a failed ioctl remains unverifiable unless host PID absence is proved. Shutdown owner/incarnation enforcement is opt-in for compatibility and checks both the authenticated grant and host record. Pane retirement precedes kill; immediate mode waits a bounded physical-exit deadline and retains unresolved ownership, graceful mode sends TERM then bounded KILL. sendSignal uses a fixed allowlist and SIGWINCH foreground-group routing. Clear/history/startup-authority mutations require their documented IDs, not invented stronger schemas.
Revive trusts cast serialized entries, skips failed PID probes/native absence, spawns a new incarnation rather than reattaching the old process and does not fabricate an attested owner; per-entry override failures skip while default failures can abort the loop. Consumer open checks protocol/session context, commits or rolls back the published grant before closing displaced delivery, and ack/pause/cancel identify exact grant/generation. Delivery cancellation is not PTY exit. Preserve RP-R1's defect: a false intake-cancellation result is ignored by a normal SSH caller before retirement/deletion; no report converts that false proof into exited.
testObligations: Attested match vs forged/no-grant/revived/legacy; spawn cancellation after physical creation; duplicate operation from another client; TERM/KILL refusal and live/unverifiable/exited; already-aborted clone/spawn; same-host PID reincarnation; delivery replacement rollback; exact false cancellation return.
contracts.downstreamBoundary: E1 owns terminal UI lifetime; WP-ENG-REMOTE owns native process discovery/signalling, SSH launch/transport and full PTY mechanics outside the listed public-body ranges.

contracts.title: Skill installation and plugin call admission
contracts.contract:
Skill schemas parse before the service wrapper. Host home/state/upload staging is authoritative; payload workspace identity is not transport authentication. Install and bundle install pass AbortSignal and remove progress listeners in finally. Startup recovery logs failure and continues; list waits for recovery, while upload begin/chunk/commit/cancel do not. Preview/remove do not pass a cancellation signal. The download origin is a fixed HTTPS role; no old destination is migrated by this audit. Upload identity is consumed by the staged installer and stable archive errors are preserved.
Plugin calls use fixed panel/worker transport plus shape and plugin context/policy checks. Crucially, current RelayRuntimeServices supplies a resolver that always returns null and null services, so these registered methods are unavailable in this production composition; registration is not an existing granted capability.
testObligations: Stage/upload cancellation and wrong upload identity; recovery failure then list/install; progress listener throws/teardown; invalid archive stable category; panel/worker with absent context and unavailable service.
contracts.downstreamBoundary: Shared transactional installer/download/native extraction remain their existing WP-ENG-INSTALL contracts; no real SSH installation executed.

contracts.title: Root registration, grace shutdown, hooks and CLI forwarding
contracts.contract:
Runtime services wire one bulk Git response registry into FS/Git and connect filesystem removal fences to PTY shutdown. Root registration accepts truthy cast fields and writes context without new handler auth; FS/Git compatibility does not consume those roots as containment. CLI/postOutput forwards params unchanged to another client excluding origin, with timeout but no forwarded signal; E4/E3 own execution/schema. Owned disposal awaits skills then AiVault with logged errors; generic registered handlers are not automatically all disposed.
Grace configuration is registered in both lanes. Number(value), finite/nonnegative, floor(seconds)*1000 means null/empty-string can select zero; invalid values retain the previous setting. Only changed, armed, non-shutdown timers re-arm, preserving deferred-shutdown state. Zero means unlimited for live PTYs; empty detached startup/idle/deferred shutdown use bounded branches. SIGTERM/INT shuts down PTYs → owned processes → pooled subscriptions → runtime → exit, SIGHUP is ignored. Failure clears in-flight state and retries only under the no-socket-client condition; retry is not physical exit proof.
Reuse RP-W1's actual WSL guest filesystem, running-distro cache, sentinel/plugin install and reconnect contracts and the initial independent relay review for managed hooks; guest host/distro/sentinel ownership and mixed versions remain. No accepted WSL census is repeated.
testObligations: Null/empty/nonnumeric grace; unchanged value cannot prolong timer; pending spawn prevents idle cap; shutdown refusal retries; CLI relay timeout without remote cancellation; missing root or forged root; WSL stopped/unverifiable distro and sentinel generation.
contracts.downstreamBoundary: Managed-hook general implementations and CLI execution remain existing owner reports; host process shutdown and WSL installation are unrun platform obligations.

contracts.title: Speech selectors, models, permissions and dictation lifecycle
contracts.contract:
Eight RPC methods validate bounded base64 audio and positive finite sample rates; they do not force every sample rate to 16kHz. Dictation receives caller ownership, whereas catalog/model actions are global. Lazy model/STT factories can produce speech_unavailable; replacing factories resets references without disposing prior services, and modelsDir is cached. Catalog readiness and configured voice/model selection are separate. Local download returns started before background completion, and failures log. Selecting a model persists before the subsequent catalog read can fail. Deletion validates writable local model, prepares STT, deletes files, then clears selection only if it still names that model.
Mobile dictation requires enabled/ready model and clientId, owns one session, validates dictationId/client/optional connection, converts PCM16 to float (dropping an odd trailing byte), and feeds only active state. Finish enters closing, stops and joins texts, then clears. Wrong-owner cancel is a no-op; right-owner cancel invokes stop, so a cloud session's cancel may finish transcription rather than discard it. Disconnect starts cancellation without awaiting it. STT claims a starting owner, rejects foreign owners and lets the same starting owner return without awaiting readiness. Cloud keys are obtained at finish through a key-reader function. Local worker reuse requires matching model/hotwords; readiness/stop timers, cancelled-owner tombstones, shared stop promise and warm reuse remain. Worker termination requested on timeout is not exit proof.
Model paths must stay under catalog-owned directories. Migration is awaited by readers; duplicate download IDs no-op, existing-file validation checks size, fresh staging downloads verify each hash before rename. Cancellation aborts without waiting; deletion removes current/staging/archive/migration sources after preparation and cancellation. Progress subscribers are not universally guarded. Desktop IPC stamps a desktop sender/session owner and performs macOS microphone status/request/recheck before start; hotword cache files are content-hashed and cleaned on terminal lifecycle paths. Native capture, keychain/provider requests and worker binaries are downstream host boundaries.
testObligations: Model switch during delete; download hash/size mismatch and cancel/delete race; missing custom credential; wrong dictation owner/connection; cloud cancel transcribes vs intended discard; same-owner concurrent start; macOS denied/restricted permission; real PCM/worker stop timeout and packaged paths.
contracts.downstreamBoundary: G15 custom provider internals, native model execution/download, microphone capture and OS/keychain integration remain named source/runtime boundaries; no built-in-only reduction or credential values.

contracts.title: Emulator selectors, host permission and managed lifecycle
contracts.contract:
Nineteen RPC methods are distinct from the ten preload stream/UI methods. Schemas bound coordinates and gesture lengths, require host-absolute artifact paths, and preserve accepted empty-string edges; logcat count is positive without a maximum. Handlers add no new context auth. Attach is feature gated and selects explicit device, configured default, then iOS default/first booted device; SDK location is supplied per Android command. Workspace normalization supports folders and deletion. Reuse avoids stopping the same active device; switching can keep Android alive, acquires a lease and rechecks workspace existence, cleaning unused startup on deletion. Managed registration and UI notification follow successful attach; no context cancellation signal is threaded through this seam.
Explicit device selection overrides workspace selection; managedOnly applies to workspace/no-explicit-device cleanup, not an explicit device shutdown. Backend selection uses ownsDevice then supported-host fallback. iOS alone backs listRunningHelpers; listAllDevices combines both. iOS advertises accessibility but not Android install/launch/permission/logcat actions. Managed references are detached before cleanup, shared workspace use prevents teardown, and lease cleanup guards concurrent starts. kill stops helper; shutdown also stops the device. Quit attempts only managed cleanup and swallows failures before clearing records, which is not proof that processes exited.
Android uses serial-scoped argv; install with exit zero still rejects Failure/Error output. Permission reset is device-wide/all-apps; grant/revoke require package and permission. Launch chooses explicit activity or Monkey, accessibility dump reads a fixed device XML only after successful dump, logcat is one-shot. No caller AbortSignal is forwarded by these immediate operations. iOS lazily materializes its helper on macOS; stop catches errors, so an apparently successful return may leave host liveness unverifiable.
testObligations: Explicit vs configured/default selection; folder deleted during attach; two workspace references; explicit device with managedOnly; unsupported capability; Android permission reset scope; zero-exit install Failure text; iOS helper stop refusal; platform permission/render/stream recovery on actual devices.
contracts.downstreamBoundary: Native backend start/retry, serveSim materializer, adb/simctl/helper binaries and rendered stream internals remain exact backend owners beyond reviewed immediate ranges; E1 owns UI streams.

contracts.title: Assignment, admission, activity, fence and drain state
contracts.contract:
The leaf table covers 63 unique public method names (not its advertised 62), plus two private helpers and one exported function: 66 rows, with no unmatched public method in the bounded class comparison. The leaf read the full 8463-line file; the lead independently read the table, nine actual assertion bodies and load-bearing assignment/renewal/claim/reservation ranges, not every line twice. The companion preserves the complete table by fingerprint/reference and the overriding lead corrections below.
The store trusts an already-authenticated caller identity from RP-C1 app routes; it is not a JWT verifier. Its owned state comprises assignments/epochs, admission/inventory, activity leases and reservation debt, runtime incarnation/heartbeat, durable fence attempts/evidence/invocations, drain attempts/receipts/pins and regional-rehome attempts/control/quarantine. Assignment placement serializes and lock-retries with general→all inventory escalation when a row appears; sticky paths differ. Conditional atomic reservation updates reject missing cell and capacity overflow. Assignment/activity fences match identity, cell, epoch and active migration; release/expiry protect durable rehome/drain pins. Control renewal bypasses the process queue and selects a six-CTE Postgres statement or transactional generic path, checking authoritative cell, exact lease kind/cell and monotonic expiry.
Fence prepare binds one live attempt to exact incarnation/base evidence, plan generation is write-once, apply binds invocation/reason, operation is write-once and attestation checks operation, disabled/stale exact incarnation before committing the fence; abort refuses once apply may have started. A refreshed heartbeat clears stale fence records. Drain prepared → send-may-have-started → application receipt is distinct from proven nondelivery; receipt-relative retry waits grace+30s, same/cross-incarnation recovery has durable once-only gates, and migration pins keep work from expiry-driven erasure. beginCellDrainSend repairs exact accounting mismatch then retries once. Evacuation preserves source/target activity ownership, registration vs active control, reservation accounting and fence evidence; no heartbeat loss is relabelled proof of process exit. Regional rehome gives retry/redrain/fresh candidates ordered priority, checks fresh locked fleet safety, claims durably before send, rate limits, pauses after repeated dispatch failure and requires CAS re-enable. Contention is swallowed only at its documented boundary; database-level transaction retries still exist.
testObligations: All 63 public contracts via full retained cloud suite; capacity overflow rolls back counters; fence binding/operation mismatch/expiry reattestation; begin-send accounting repair; receipt vs nondelivery; locked inventory escalation; renewed control in both SQL dialects; rehome redrain/three-failure CAS; mixed-version lock ordering.
contracts.downstreamBoundary: D-CLOUD-COLLAB retains six external selector/registration/headroom/queue/safety/abandonment implementations as explicit source boundaries. RP-C1/C2 retain public route/admin/fence-broker authentication. No whole cloud-state implementation closure.

contracts.title: Cloud relay WebSocket admission
contracts.contract: Upgrade routing refuses query strings, decodes and validates relay host identity, applies per-route capacity/rate admission and restricts host connections to data-cell mode. Phone capacity is reserved before rate checks and released once; first-frame auth is separate from socket registration. Control tokens are asynchronously verified before control ledger admission. Invite director routing can persist an assignment before forwarding/move. Malformed first payloads are caught. Socket error guards log errors, they are not no-ops. Client-address extraction relies on the expected reverse proxy's forwarding provenance; trusting a penultimate XFF hop does not itself authenticate public callers. Closing WebSocket server objects is not proof that all sessions/processes ended.
testObligations: Upgrade query/host mismatch; phone reserve then rate rejection; first auth malformed/token rejected; async control admission race; director move after durable assignment; forged forwarding header at actual ingress; close while authenticated sessions live.
contracts.downstreamBoundary: Phone/host session implementations and public proxy/IAM configuration remain separately named session and O-INFRA-OPS owners; accepted RP-C1 route authentication is reused.

contracts.title: Database dialect, transaction and failure boundary
contracts.contract: Database boot chooses PostgreSQL from configured URL or SQLite WAL, applies schema/backfills, and best-effort closes on failed open. No connection values are reproduced. SQLite queues transactions via a promise tail, then executes BEGIN IMMEDIATE before the try/finally that releases it: BEGIN failure can leave later transactions blocked. Nested transaction wrappers use the same client and do not establish a savepoint. PostgreSQL acquires a fresh pooled client, rolls back on error and releases in finally; recognized deadlock/serialization/lock SQLSTATEs retry with 0..25ms jitter. Pool acquisition is outside the retry try. Other transient classification is broader than actual retry policy. Callbacks may run again; external effects cannot be assumed exactly-once. Locked queries add FOR UPDATE/NOWAIT or a bounded local lock timeout and restore best-effort. Placeholder replacement is lexical, not a SQL parser.
testObligations: SQLite BEGIN throws then next transaction; callback/commit/rollback failure; pool acquisition vs retry; nested rollback semantics; each SQLSTATE retry/exhaustion; lock timeout restoration and client reuse; Postgres/SQLite control renewal equivalence.
contracts.downstreamBoundary: Database source1–1024 independently read including DDL, query and boot branches. Imported applyPostgresSchema, pool-pressure/hold metrics and driver implementations remain owner interfaces; no actual database migration or SQL execution.

contracts.title: Regional rehome worker dispatch lifecycle
contracts.contract: Only a configured director with audience/service-account/safety snapshot activates the periodic jittered worker. An in-flight guard prevents overlapping ticks. The store claims durable identity/attempt/source incarnation/epoch before the worker obtains a service token and POSTs host drain with a 10s deadline. Only the documented accepted/already-accepted/host-not-connected receipt shapes commit the corresponding store result; errors record dispatch/worker failure best-effort and log. stop clears future scheduling; it does not cancel an in-flight claim, token acquisition, fetch or receipt write. Registration/receipt does not prove migration convergence.
testObligations: Disabled/missing role prerequisites; overlapping tick; stop during fetch; token failure after claim; malformed/non-success receipt; failure-accounting write also fails; accepted receipt but host still dual-homed.
contracts.downstreamBoundary: Google identity-token minting/verifier and source-cell drain service are external owned boundaries from RP-C1/C2; no token or request was used.

contracts.title: Multi-target deployment-operation control entry
contracts.contract:
The parser selects eleven modes with mode-specific target counts, exact source/target topology, selector generation/attempt/capacity bounds and a 40-hex fence commit. It validates environment and HTTPS drain audience; unknown paired flags are not globally rejected. Normal administration uses its audience-bound token role, with a separate broker token for fence paths. Abort-fence/selector-inspection return early; cutover/add/promote/retire have distinct selector/CAS sequences. Audit/preflight return after their checks, not after deployment.
Recover-forward repeats bounded catch-up, publishes migrations before source existing-only/target migration-only admission, and checks durable send-permit state/expiry before drain and receipt. Legacy shouldSend differs from prepared send. Reissue requires fresh incarnation/ownership/lease proof; convergence waits migration completion, zero activity and source-final state. Execute delegates evacuation, while fencing ties source generation, commit/plan/apply/operation/attestation before destructive infrastructure work. Failure does not imply rollback or host exit. The lead independently read all3135 lines, including local helper bodies. Resource selection refuses overlap in origin/MIG/group/backend; selector cutover requires a single100% active revision and isolated0% rollback with identical image/inventory, a minimum floor, then prunes incompatible revisions. Readiness compares runtime/director connection policy, finite counts and headroom before assigning greedy least-loaded quotas. Capacity snapshots use two rounds, three attempts; recovery uses conservative min/max rules rather than pretending one atomic snapshot. Runtime log fallback requires90s freshness. Route inspection compares backend, URL map, proxy, forwarding rule/address and DNS. Migration publication validates each returned batch count; recovery alone tolerates depleted/headroom-paused quotas.
Before drain, rollback refuses to act without known registration status, preserves forward recovery after any target registration, and preserves an active selector. drainAttempted becomes true before send-permit acquisition, so later failure cannot trigger ordinary rollback. Recovery completion permits only the documented bounded-unregistered case; fencing requires strict full coverage and zero source work, with fresh pre-apply and post-apply generation/route/target checks. Terraform orchestration selects completed-commit recovery, safe supersede, resume, legacy adoption or fresh apply and passes plan/state bindings plus invocation/operation/attestation callbacks. Abort delegates proof that apply never started before deleting plans. Failed-target supersession fences that target, checks replacement capacity, loops validated batch counts and demands final registration/count reconciliation; the loop has no own total deadline. Imported Terraform helper implementations remain a deliberate external boundary.

contracts.title: Staging power operational ordering
contracts.contract:
Topology validation constrains staging cell roles/counts; a token-shaped string check is not cryptographic verification. If SQL is already off, sleep refuses any running cell and only reconciles an all-stopped state. Otherwise it first checks every cell quiescent and refuses selector generation greater than zero; only then sleep disables admission and waits 15s BEFORE entering the catch-protected phase. That guarded phase verifies disabled admission/quiescence, scales Cloud Run minimum to zero and rechecks quiescence; it best-effort re-enables on failure. MIG resizing to zero and SQL activation policy NEVER occur AFTER the catch. Therefore neither initial disable failure nor MIG/SQL failure has the claimed global rollback. Cloud Run may no-op when active revision minimum is zero, not necessarily after latest-revision convergence.
Wake sets SQL ALWAYS, waits director health, keeps Cloud Run minimum zero, selects active/legacy topology, restores cells, waits readiness and verifies heartbeat/admission. Active selector mode restores retained cells; legacy may target a subset. No general rollback or child-process timeout exists around synchronous CLI calls.
testObligations: Failure at each step of disable/guarded phase/MIG/SQL; partial admission rollback; active-vs-latest revision drift; wake health timeout; stale selector/cell heartbeat; stopped child or unavailable CLI.
contracts.downstreamBoundary: Actual SQL/MIG/Cloud Run identities/resources and IAM effects belong O-INFRA-OPS; source ordering is reviewed without executing any operation.

contracts.title: Infrastructure command dispatch seam
contracts.contract: The entry chooses IAC_TOOL or searches installed tools before validating command/environment. It checks environment truthiness, not a staging|production enum, despite usage text. Root lookup uses the in operator and therefore has prototype-property edges before later path guards. It interpolates backend/variable paths and requires their existence. init, plan and apply are separate dispatch branches (no automatic init-before-plan); apply consumes the saved plan, and the staging relay apply guard is specific to that literal environment/root. Credential roles are explicit environment-supplied tool auth or a gcloud token fallback; no value is copied. This characterizes command dispatch only, not Terraform state/IAM/resource correctness.
testObligations: Invalid/prototype root; missing/arbitrary environment; missing tool before usage refusal; missing files; saved-plan provenance and stale plan; staging guard; credential fallback unavailable.

ranges.testName: latches off after three dispatch failures and resumes only through CAS

ranges.testName: redrains a receipted dual-homed attempt once its grace elapses

ranges.testName: keeps a brand-new assignment retry scoped to general admission

ranges.testName: restarts with full inventory if an assignment appears during a general retry
